questions.question: Which one of the following is true about mixed economy?

options.text: Existence of both developed and underdeveloped sectors
Equal importance to agriculture and industry
Existence of both public and private sectors in national economy
Equal partnership of central and states in economic planning and development

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Existence of both public and private sectors in national economy**__

__
 
• The main feature of a mixed economy is the co-existence of both public and private enterprises__.
 
• They work together. The industries in the private sector are managed and operated completely by private entrepreneurs. 
 
• On the other-hand there is the public sector in which the enterprises are owned and managed by the State.

questions.question: Which among the following is the most appropriate measure of an economic growth of a country?
questions.solution:
Per capita income or average income measures the average income earned per person in a given area in a specified year. It is calculated by dividing the area's total income by its total population.

The per capita GDP is especially useful when comparing one country to another, because it shows the relative performance of the countries.

questions.question:

questions.question: Who is also known as 'Light of Asia'?
questions.solution:
Gautam Buddha is called “Light of Asia”. It is the title of a book written by Sir Edwin Arnold about the life of Buddha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Mahatma Buddha was born on the day of Vaishakh Purnima in 563 BC in **Lumbini,** located in the lowlands of Nepal.
 
• It is well known that in his youth he saw the miseries of human life like sick person, old age and death. On the contrary, influenced by a happy sannyasin, Buddha at the age of 29 renounced worldly life and set out in search of truth.
 
• Mahatma Buddha attained self-realization while meditating under a Peepal tree in Bodh Gaya on the day of Vaishakh Purnima in 528 BC.
 
• On the day of Vaishakh Purnima, in **483 BC**, Mahatma Buddha attained Nirvana at a place called Kushinara.
 
• After his death, his disciples called a council at Rajagriha, where the main teachings of Buddhism were codified.
 
• Four Buddhist councils were organized to synergize these teachings in the form of pitakas, after which three main pitakas were formed.
 
• The **Vinaya Pitaka** (the rules of order for Buddhists), **the Sutta Pitaka** (the teaching principles of the Buddha) and **the Abhidhamma Pitaka** (Buddhist philosophy), are collectively referred to as the **Tripitaka.** All these have been written in **Pali language**.

questions.question: Near coastal areas, temperature on land in night time gets reduced due to ________.
questions.solution:
• Near coastal areas, the temperature on land in night time gets reduced due to Land breeze.
 
• Land breezes usually occur at night. At night, the temperature of the land cools quickly without the insolation from the sun.
 
• Heat is rapidly re-radiated back to the surrounding air. The water along the shore will then be warmer than the coastal land, creating a net movement of air from the land surfaces towards the ocean.

questions.question: Which of the following wind is also known as 'Snow Eater'?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Chinook**__ wind is also known as 'Snow Eater’ as these winds move east, they rise over the western slopes of the mountains and then descend, becoming extremely dry and much warmer.
 
• Air naturally warms as it sinks, but dry air warms almost twice as fast as moist air.
 
• The winds can also spread fires easily because of the extremely dry air.

questions.question: Turmeric is a modified _____.
questions.solution: A rhizome ("mass of roots”) is a modified stem that grows horizontally underground. It has nodes and internodes. Vertical shoots may arise from the buds on the rhizome of some plants, such as turmeric or ginger.

questions.question: What is the nature of cell membrane?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Semi-Permeable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A Semi-permeable cell membrane is one that allows certain molecules or ions to pass through it by means of active or passive transport.
 
• Active transport processes require the cell to expend energy to move the materials, while passive transport can be done without using cellular energy.
 
• Surrounding the cell membrane in most plants, fungi, algae, and bacteria, the cell wall is a semi-permeable layer.
 
• It is responsible for providing structure, support, and protection to the cell.

questions.question: Law of Inertia is also known as _____
questions.solution: Newton's first law is also known as the "law of inertia." This law states that if an object is at rest, then it will stay at rest until it is acted upon by another object. Then, the law states that an object in motion will stay in motion unless it is acted upon by an unbalanced force.

questions.question: Surface water of a lake is about to freeze. What will be the temperature (in °C) of water at the bottom of the lake?
questions.solution:
• The temperature of water at the bottom of the lake will be 4°centigrade. As the water density increases, there is a decrease in freezing point.
 
• Hence the ice cannot be seen at the bottom of the lakes or oceans as the water at the bottom of the lake has more density than the top level.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes used in automatic vehicles is direct virtual application of which law?
questions.solution: A hydraulic brake is an arrangement of braking mechanism which uses brake fluid, typically containing glycol ethers or diethylene glycol, to transfer pressure from the controlling mechanism to the braking mechanism.Pascal's law basically states that any pressure applied to a fluid inside a closed system will transmit that pressure equally in all directions throughout the fluid. This law is the basic principle that causes hydraulic power in heavy construction machines to work.

questions.question:
Which among the following is/are input devices?

I. Keyboard

II. Scanner

III. Joy-stick
questions.solution:
**Keyboard**: A computer keyboard is an input device that allows a person to enter letters, numbers, and other symbols (these are called characters) into a computer.

**Scanner**: A scanner is an input device that scans documents such as photographs and pages of text. 

**Joy-stick**: A joystick is an input device consisting of a stick that pivots on a base and reports its angle or direction to the device it is controlling.

questions.question: Which of the following is used as moderator in atomic reactor?
